subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should third-party plugin manifests be allowed to propose install-time changes outside `plugins.entries.<id>.config`, and what consent, allowed-surface, conflict, provenance, and recovery guarantees must apply?
rationale: Source evidence establishes that the capability is missing, but repository behavior alone cannot determine how much authority untrusted plugin metadata should receive over user-owned core configuration.

options.title: Constrained config intents
options.body: Add typed, auditable setup operations with explicit user review, validation, provenance, and recovery rather than accepting arbitrary JSON deep-merges.

options.title: Plugin-scoped config only
options.body: Limit automatic writes to `plugins.entries.<id>.config` and use documented setup or onboarding flows for core provider, tool, hook, and channel settings.

options.title: Keep configuration explicit
options.body: Reject manifest-driven config mutation and improve Control UI and CLI guidance so users apply security-sensitive changes themselves.

recommendation.title: Constrained config intents
recommendation.body: Add typed, auditable setup operations with explicit user review, validation, provenance, and recovery rather than accepting arbitrary JSON deep-merges.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has recent implementation history on the affected contract and the clearest recorded review of the unresolved product and security choice.
